items.q: A market was worth £380m in 2024 and £370m in 2025. What was the percentage change?
items.why: Percentage change = (new – old) ÷ old × 100 = (370 – 380) ÷ 380 × 100 = -2.6%. Divide by the old figure.
items.label: New question

items.q: A factory with 40 employees produced 31,000 units last year. What was its labour productivity?
items.why: Labour productivity = output ÷ number of employees = 31,000 ÷ 40 = 775 units per employee per year.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business has non-current liabilities of £350,000 and gearing of 40%. It takes out a new long-term loan of £100,000. What is its new gearing?
items.why: Capital employed before = £350,000 ÷ 40% = £875,000. The loan adds to both non-current liabilities and capital employed. New gearing = (£350,000 + £100,000) ÷ (£875,000 + £100,000) × 100 = 46.2%.

items.q: The chart shows DT's usual pattern of inventory control. Calculate the re-order quantity.
items.why: Each delivery takes inventory from the buffer level of 750 units up to the maximum of 6,000 units. Re-order quantity = 6,000 – 750 = 5,250 units.
items.label: Paper 2 June 2022 Q03.2

items.q: A business has 100 employees who are each expected to work 230 days a year. 340 working days were lost to absence. What is the absenteeism rate?
items.why: Absenteeism = days lost ÷ total possible working days × 100 = 340 ÷ (100 × 230) × 100 = 340 ÷ 23,000 × 100 = 1.48%.

items.q: Revenue £15m, Cost of sales £7m, Other expenses £9m, Taxation £2m. Gross profit = ?
items.why: Gross profit = Revenue - Cost of Sales = 15 - 7 = £8m. Other expenses and taxation are not deducted for gross profit. Only deduct Cost of Sales for gross profit. nothing else.

items.q: The chart shows DT's usual pattern of inventory control. Calculate the lead time.
items.why: Inventory reaches the reorder level of 2,150 units on day 11 and the delivery arrives on day 15. Lead time = 15 – 11 = 4 days.

items.q: A business has sales of £100m in a market worth £806m. What is its market share?
items.why: Market share = business sales ÷ total market sales × 100 = 100 ÷ 806 × 100 = 12.4%.
items.label: New question

items.q: A company has non-current liabilities of £60m and total equity of £110m. What is its gearing?
items.why: Capital employed = total equity + non-current liabilities = £110m + £60m = £170m. Gearing = non-current liabilities ÷ capital employed × 100 = 60 ÷ 170 × 100 = 35.3%.
